references.text: Balak repeats his promise to give Balaam great honor, showing the king's desperation to have the people cursed
Balak again refers to the honor he would have given Balaam, but which the Lord withheld from him
God's promise to Abraham to curse those who curse his descendants, relevant to Balak's desire to curse Israel
The Lord turned Balaam's curse into a blessing, showing that Balak's plan failed
Proverbs warn against letting wealth and honor lead to sin, relevant to Balak's offer of great honor
Satan tempts Jesus with the kingdoms of the world and their glory, a similar temptation to what Balak offered Balaam
Jesus teaches that it profits nothing to gain the whole world yet lose one's soul, relevant to Balaam's temptation
Peter mentions the way of Balaam as an example of greed and error
Jude warns against those who have rushed into Balaam's way for profit's sake
John refers to the teaching of Balaam as a warning to the church in Pergamon
